answer: At a wharf where AI agents bid for cargo, each agent must lock a refundable pearl of collateral in a shared contract before bidding. Voting power is proportional to collateral, not the number of identities, so splitting one stake among a thousand agents gains no influence. To gain more influence, an attacker must lock more capital; if a bid is provably fraudulent, the contract can slash the stake, pushing the attacker’s return toward its nadir.
